legs.detail: The post-Solution-A re-snapshot wave over the Dossier 06 A1 scope in A2's order (the 5 missing re-captures and the named never-captured set first, then the homepage and core files, all dataset files, all dataset landings, the five takeover category pages, the live blog set, the API root). Polite runner: batches of at most 5, at least 30 s between saves, at least 3 min between batches. Observed throttle behaviour: the Archive throttled the save responses' content leg with HTTP 429 throughout, while the saves themselves landed server-side — every throttled save that was re-checked appeared in CDX, the same pattern the 2026-10-30 program record documents. A capture is counted only on CDX evidence (timestamp, status, CDX digest, record length); submitted-but-unconfirmed saves are exceptions below, never rounded up.

Sampled wave captures fetched in id_ identity form: bytes re-hash (SHA-1, Wayback digest form) to their CDX digests — the captures are the indexed bytes, unaltered; and (SHA-256) against the signed index named above for data files and against the public route documents for pages — the currency leg. Sampled rows are itemized in the batch evidence (runbook-evidence.json) and the sampled captures carry the digest-verified era basis in the registry.

The A2 enumeration executed over the full sitemap plus the tracked non-sitemap surfaces (260 targets) before the wave and again after it: capture states are computed from CDX data, never sampled. Before: no current-era capture existed anywhere on the estate. After: every wave-scope URL carries a current-era capture or stands in an explicit exception state.

One retry of the Zenodo v1.2.0 record page (https://zenodo.org/records/23844324), per the E6-B2 scope. The save response itself was throttled (HTTP 429, the content-leg pattern seen across the wave); the outcome recorded here is the post-wave CDX sweep's verdict, not the immediate post-save check. The v1.1.0 record page's failure history (six HTTP 520s) stands in the E6-B1 report; preservation of both records is by DOI regardless of the Wayback outcome (Dossier 06 A3).

conclusion: The re-snapshot wave archived the current (per-route) byte era of the estate across the designed scope: 103 of 103 wave URLs hold CDX-confirmed current-era captures (99 confirmed against their wave saves, 4 confirmed on verify-first re-check after throttled save responses), and 20/20 sampled captures re-hash to their CDX digests in id_ form. Exceptions are confined to 0 recorded items (itemized above); no copy was overwritten and no unconfirmed save is counted anywhere.
